races.name: Spillers Future Champions Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up operator trained by Charlie Johnston, 12 days fresh and carrying 138lbs; nine runs on similar going show consistent placing (0W4P) but no win, which is a concern in a race that may come down to one explosive moment — needs luck in running on the Epsom camber.
runners_data.comment: Qitaal arrives here in fine fettle after a run just 12 days ago, boasting experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 81 marks him out as the one to beat in this field; the chief concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts despite a string of placings.

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Six-year-old held up by Gary & Moore combination, wears a tongue tie, and boasts three wins from 11 similar-ground runs — the most potent winning record in this field on comparable conditions; 29 days since last run is manageable and the return to 10f after a stint over shorter trips is a positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Oj Lifestyle won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with a 29-day break leaving him fresh. Carrying 136 lb from stall one, he rates competitive on our figures and commands respect off an official mark of 73.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Genuine deep hold-up performer with a visor, whose true preference for the rear means the midfield map position overstates his actual likely spot in running; 1W4P on similar going, best efforts over 12f-16f suggest this 10f trip may be a touch sharp, and the Best yard is quiet (0/6 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing five-year-old who won on firm going over 10f and has four placed efforts on good ground — the headgear and recent 14-day return suggest the Birkett team have him primed; though he races in a nominal midfield slot, his true hold-up style means he needs traffic to part cleanly in the Epsom straight.
runners_data.comment: Show Biz Kid landed a win three starts back but has managed only a third and a fifth since, and ranked fifth of six on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Magical Merlin
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's six-year-old returns after 59 days off, the longest absence in this field, which is worth noting though Charlton has a runner here within a live fitness window; placed twice on softer ground over shorter trips, the step back up to 10f is interesting but the form has faded recently (845 in last three) and the deep hold-up style is difficult to execute from a nominal midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last five starts — a fourth two starts back and seconds four and five starts back — Magical Merlin brings distance-and-going experience and a rating of 74 that marks him as a live threat, though 59 days off the track is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Mark Hoad's six-year-old, lightly supported trainer (0/1 in 14 days) but the horse shows two wins and five placings across 11 similar-going efforts; back up to 10f after a 12f run, the form shows a level consistency (3-4-6 range) that makes it competitive without suggesting a decisive winning move — positional fortune in the straight will be key.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fifth last time out and no finish better than third in recent starts, Bobacious is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: This is an entirely hold-up field at Epsom over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground, meaning there is no natural front-runner to set a genuine gallop — the race is near-certain to crawl into the straight before erupting into a frantic sprint finish from the three-furlong pole. Qitaal and Oj Lifestyle are the two truest hold-up types and will settle at the rear with minimal fuss, while Golden Circet, Show Biz Kid, Magical Merlin, and Bobacious are all redistributed hold-up horses mapped to midfield simply because the field has more rear-runners than the map can accommodate. The crawl-and-sprint nature of Epsom's 1m2f trip — with its sharp turns and camber — heavily favours horses who can quicken off a slow pace and handle the track's unique demands, making the premium runner profile one of tactical awareness, a sharp finishing kick, and clean passage through a tightly-bunched field. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the rear of the map shows, and of those pushed into a nominal midfield role, Show Biz Kid (wears a hood, recent course-distance form, consistent on good ground) and Golden Circet (wide-draw handler, proven over this trip) are best placed to secure the most forward actual position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the race crawls as expected and erupts into a mass sprint from the three-furlong pole, favoured runners are those with the sharpest turn of foot on good-to-firm Epsom ground.
scenarios.body: The slow early pace compresses the field into a cluster entering the straight, and Epsom's cambered track rewards those who find a clean line and produce a late surge; horses with proven good-ground form over this trip will dominate. Qitaal's consistent placing record on good going and Oj Lifestyle's three wins at similar conditions make them the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to track slightly closer than their natural role and pounces with a well-timed run through the Epsom camber.
scenarios.body: Show Biz Kid's headgear (hood) and recent 10f good-ground form, including a win at similar conditions, gives it an edge if it sits just off the slow pace in a genuine midfield berth and produces a clean run. Golden Circet, proven over 10f-12f trips on good going with a placed effort at a similar level, could also exploit this shape if given an unobstructed passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injection Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one horse breaks the pattern and injects pace from halfway, stringing the field out and suiting a horse that can handle the pressure and sustain a longer run.
scenarios.body: A sudden injection of pace from the turn would punish horses that settle too deeply and benefit any runner able to latch onto the move early; Bobacious, whose form shows consistent midfield to placed efforts over 10f on good ground, could profit from a longer-run scenario. Magical Merlin, dropped back from shorter trips and trained by Harry Charlton who has a runner here within a manageable return window, could find this shape playing to a more sustained gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Scrimmage, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide entering the straight, causing interference and crowding, with the winner emerging from a confused finish.
scenarios.body: Epsom's tight camber and a six-runner hold-up field creates genuine risk of a muddled finish where positional luck determines the result; any horse drawn to find a clear outer berth without traffic would benefit disproportionately. Oj Lifestyle's experience (6-year-old, 15 similar-going runs) and Qitaal's course familiarity give both a marginal edge if the finish devolves into positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a falsely slow early gallop — with no natural front-runner in the field, the pace could be dangerously sedate entering Tattenham Corner, dramatically compressing the field and turning the finish into pure positional lottery.

Qitaal and Oj Lifestyle are both true hold-up types on the highest weights (138lbs and 136lbs respectively) — monitor whether the top weights can quicken as sharply as the lighter-framed runners when the sprint erupts.

Show Biz Kid's hood (first-time or reapplied headgear) could make it fractious or keen early — if it races away from its hold-up role and burns energy before the straight, its chance is materially compromised.

Golden Circet's best form has come at 12f-16f; watch whether Warren Fentiman elects to press forward to compensate for the shorter trip, which would be a significant change in race shape if it happens.
Magical Merlin has the longest lay-off at 59 days and drops back from 8f recent runs to 10f — watch the market moves closer to post time for any stable confidence signals given the fitness query.

races.name: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Out Of This World
runners_data.note: Clear pace angle here — sole confirmed front-runner on a track that rewards leaders, James Tate yard in fair recent form (1/14 over 14 days), ran 1W1P in similar going, steps up to 7f from 8f runs, the 44-day break is the one question mark but hg headgear suggests she can travel kindly.

runners_data.name: Banged Up
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends out a filly who showed a fade on debut over 6f at Goodwood; true running style is hold-up but with the rear end crowded she will likely be shuffled into mid-division, and her finishing effort on that debut form (coded 0) offers little encouragement at present.

runners_data.name: Camarda Rc
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner with no public form — completely unknown quantity — Seamus Cronin claims 5lbs which aids the weight, and Hannon debuts horses to compete, so the absence of a form string should not be taken as a negative without further context.

runners_data.name: Cool King
runners_data.note: Marco Botti runner who ran a modest 7th on debut over 6f at Sandown; stepping up to 7f which may help given his hold-up profile, but sim-going record is a single run with no wins or places and Neil Callan will need a willing traveller to get into this from the rear.

runners_data.name: Otis Bay
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace debut runner, Jack Nicholls (3) in the plate — Eustace is a 3/12 trainer over 14 days suggesting solid strike rate, and this horse's unknown style means the going report of Good to Firm is neither a confirmed advantage nor a concern until seen in running.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Galore
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly has form over 6f and 7f in good ground — the step back to 7f (after an 8th over that trip last time) is a slight concern, but she has genuine hold-up credentials and the 13-day turnaround suggests she is in a good place physically; her best chance comes if pace is strong enough to draw her through.

runners_data.name: Benefacta
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes filly whose best form (a 3rd over 6f in good ground) came on her debut; she is a genuine hold-up horse who will be forced into the midfield pack by the crowded rear end, which is not her preferred scenario — the two softer-ground runs since that debut are also a mild going query.

runners_data.name: Aminaty
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding sends this Andrew Balding runner back after 21 days, and Daniel Muscutt is a competent booking, but two runs over 7f in good ground both produced finishes of 7th and 11th — the lack of progress in identical conditions is a genuine concern rather than simply a pace-map redistribution issue.

runners_data.name: Secret Flite
runners_data.note: Tom Ward trainer has 0 winners from 9 runners over 14 days — notable cold-yard stat — and this filly ran 9th on debut over 6f in good ground; Kieran O'Neill takes over from the debut rider, and the fade-in-finish flag combined with the trainer stat makes her among the hardest to recommend in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Out Of This World is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner novice field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Epsom's seven furlongs on Good to Firm ground. The remainder of the field — Banged Up, Aminaty, Benefacta, Cool King, Whiskey Galore, and Secret Flite — are all hold-up or rear-tracking types, meaning the pace is thin and the race is unlikely to be truly run. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; Out Of This World is virtually certain to secure the lead uncontested, while Banged Up, Aminaty, and Benefacta — all redistributed from their true hold-up positions — will be forced wider in the pack than their natural style dictates. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses with a turn of foot from just off the pace, as the moderate early fractions set by a lone front-runner will compress the field and make it very difficult for genuine hold-up horses to generate enough momentum from the back to overhaul a fresh-legged leader in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Out Of This World bowls along unchallenged at a controlled tempo and her rivals are unable to close the gap on the descent.
scenarios.body: Out Of This World sets the fractions entirely to her own liking, arriving at the two-furlong pole with reserves in hand while hold-up horses scramble from unpromising positions; horses with tactical flexibility or the ability to sit just behind the pace are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Quickens Field
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up runners organise themselves quickly and a strong sustained gallop from the rear creates a genuine late challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield bunch produces a wall of finishers, with runners who travel smoothly through the race benefiting most from the Epsom downhill run into the straight; horses with proven stamina for seven furlongs in good ground hold the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types — most likely Aminaty or Benefacta — secures an unplanned prominent position and times a run to challenge from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Forced out of their natural hold-up role by the lack of pace, these horses end up racing in a position that actually suits a moderate tempo scenario better than expected; the one who travels most fluently through the race rather than needing a late injection of pace will be the danger.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Field
scenarios.trigger: If the two unraced or lightly exposed runners — Camarda Rc or Otis Bay — produce a significant step forward from their debut or show natural ability superior to anything in the form book.
scenarios.body: A genuinely unexposed type encountering a soft pace scenario for the first time can outclass tired rivals who have been disadvantaged by the compressed race shape; unexposed horses from powerful yards often thrive when a steady gallop rewards raw talent over tactical experience.

watchPoints.text: Out Of This World — watch whether she settles into a natural rhythm in the early stages or is pushed along to establish her lead; if Rob Hornby has her on the bridle going into the first bend, the race could be over as a contest long before the straight.

Camarda Rc and Otis Bay — both debut runners from competent yards (Hannon, Eustace) who could produce a performance significantly above what the field expects; unknown form strings in a race of this type can distort the true market and field dynamics.

Banged Up and Aminaty — both are genuine hold-up horses remapped into midfield; watch their position in the first two furlongs, because if the pace is slow and they cannot get into a true rhythm behind a crawling leader, their chances of landing a late blow are materially reduced.

Whiskey Galore — the 13-day turnaround and a previous run over this exact trip in good ground makes her the most pace-ready of the genuine hold-up types; watch whether Ross Coakley tries to improve her position earlier than usual given the likely compressed gallop.

races.name: Spillers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 12f on standard-to-slow going and a solid similar-going record (2W6P from 9 runs) give her the most credible hold-up profile in the race; Dougie Costello is a confident booking and her trainer Tregoning fires at 1/4 over the past fortnight, but she has yet to prove herself on turf as quick as good-to-firm.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Moon has two wins in her last five starts and comes here with distance-and-going experience, fit enough at 27 days since her last run; the worry is that a fifth last time out suggests she may need things to fall right to recapture that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old wearing a tongue-tie and running for a trainer in poor current form (0/8 T14); his recent efforts show a string of sixth-place finishes and his best trip on the figures has been shorter than today's 14f, so he needs a significant step forward — the hold-up style is genuine but the data offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dream Harder nevertheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, and has run over today's trip and going — his 19-day turnaround looks sharp enough. The 133 lb burden is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the field who has won three of his last four starts including back-to-back victories; the six-day turnaround is the one flag, and he carries a STYLE_FIT tag meaning any scenario that requires him to race differently than on the pace should be discounted — he will lead and his recent form suggests he is well-equipped to do so.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Cult arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and with three wins in his last five starts — he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 128 lb is no impost for a horse in this form. The sole concern is whether six days is enough recovery.

runners_data.name: Stage Show
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good ground earlier in the season and is a genuine hold-up type by nature; redistributed to the midfield map position only because the field is saturated with rear-of-field runners, so expect him to race further back than shown — the STYLE_FIT tag and being out of natural role both temper how strongly this can be rated.
runners_data.comment: Stage Show brings solid recent form to this contest — third last time out and a winner three starts back — with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the main risk is that eighth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Two Plus Two
runners_data.note: Carries a hood and has a consistent place record over exactly 14f on good ground (2W3P from 5 runs at the trip), making the distance and going combination his clearest angle; like Stage Show he is a true hold-up horse whose map position is a redistribution artefact, and the STYLE_FIT tag means his chance is conditional on circumstances rather than design.
runners_data.comment: Two Plus Two has managed just one win in his last five starts, with a pair of fourths either side of a runner-up effort doing little to inspire confidence — he ranks last on our figures here. The distance and going experience counts in his favour, and 21 days off should leave him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Imperial Cult is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no rival willing or able to press him, he is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the outset on good-to-firm ground at Epsom. The remaining four runners — Twilight Moon, Dream Harder, Stage Show and Two Plus Two — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Imperial Cult will enjoy an uncontested lead and can govern every yard of the race at whatever tempo suits him. On a track as unique as Epsom, where Tattenham Corner and the long downhill run home reward horses in a rhythm, an uncontested pace-setter who can switch off and conserve energy is in a powerful tactical position. This race shape strongly favours Imperial Cult and any hold-up horse with the tactical speed to pick up the tempo on the descent — the field holds more true hold-up runners than the map can place at the rear, with Stage Show and Two Plus Two redistributed to midfield, but their actual finishing positions will depend on how much Imperial Cult has left in the tank turning in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Imperial Cult Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Cult is allowed to lead unchallenged and controls the tempo throughout, conserving energy for the Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: Imperial Cult sets a sustainable gallop, keeps the hold-up horses in a flat-footed chase around Tattenham Corner, and kicks clear on the descent before they can close — his recent sharp six-day turnaround and form of 1-1141 underline he is in the form of his life.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Cult fades in the straight after his recent six-day turnaround takes its toll and a hold-up horse sustains a strong run from the turn.
scenarios.body: The long Epsom straight gives a well-positioned hold-up runner time to reel in a tiring leader, and Twilight Moon's back-to-back wins at the trip on similar going make her the most plausible beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Two Plus Two or Stage Show, slotted into midfield, gets a perfect run around Tattenham Corner and arrives with a decisive late surge.
scenarios.body: Stage Show's win over 13f on good ground and Two Plus Two's consistent place record over 14f on good ground mean either could capitalise if Imperial Cult is caught out by the unique demands of Epsom — but both are racing out of their natural hold-up role which tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dream Harder Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Harder, fresh from a layoff in headgear, produces an unexpectedly strong late run to overhaul the field.
scenarios.body: Dream Harder's form figures of 666-68 and a trainer running at 0/8 in the last 14 days make this a low-probability outcome, though the step up to 14f and tongue-tie could theoretically unlock latent ability.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Cult's six-day turnaround is the single biggest race threat — watch whether Neil Callan lets him stride freely from the gate or if any sign of fatigue emerges on the descent into the straight.

Stage Show and Two Plus Two are both genuine hold-up horses squeezed into the midfield map — watch how Finley Marsh and Dylan Hogan actually position them early, as both racing wide or getting shuffled back could cost them vital ground at Tattenham Corner.
Twilight Moon's form has been on standard-to-slow artificial surfaces; watch how she handles the good-to-firm Epsom turf, as Dougie Costello may need to adjust his finishing kick timing accordingly.

With four hold-up horses chasing one front-runner, watch whether the pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field — if Imperial Cult crawls, the race could turn into a sprint from the three-furlong pole, which would suit whoever is best positioned rounding the home turn.

races.name: Irish EBF Fifinella Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chantelle
runners_data.note: Returning from 152 days off for Sir Mark Prescott, who excels with fresh horses, she is the lone genuine pace-setter and has winning form over 7f on Standard; stepping up to 1m½f on Good to Firm at Epsom is the key query, and her STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she is confirmed in the lead role rather than racing out of it — the concern is whether the trip and lay-off combine against her late.
runners_data.comment: Chantelle arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, most recently a runner-up effort, and has run over today's trip — a trainer firing at 38% in the last fortnight is a major positive; the concern is 152 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Celestra
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's filly arrives on the back of a 19-day turnaround with winning form over 8f on Good and a strong similar-going record (1W3P from 4 runs); prominent by nature and ideally positioned to track Chantelle through the race, the step up to 1m½f is the main unknown but her recent form string of 2-2318 shows consistent competitiveness.
runners_data.comment: Celestra won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing a lively recent profile over today's trip and going; she carries a hefty 133 lb but our rating of 88 marks her clear of this field and she's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has winning form over 8f on Good and three placed efforts on similar surfaces, but she too is a natural prominent type who has been mapped to the rear simply because there is no room for her at the front; her actual chance depends on how freely she settles in an unfamiliar rear position rather than on any genuine hold-up ability.
runners_data.comment: Trio arrives here on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a genuine threat; the main risk is whether she can reproduce that form under a hefty 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Too Hot To Tango
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's filly boasts a recent winning run and solid form over 10f, and her natural style is to race prominently — in this shape, however, she cannot get her preferred position and will likely race closer to midfield than she would choose, which is a meaningful tactical disadvantage; the trainer's T14 figure of 0/7 adds no short-term confidence.
runners_data.comment: Too Hot To Tango won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making her a live threat at 128 lb; the risk is that 45 days off the track leaves her fitness slightly in question.

races.paceDynamic: Chantelle is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only three rivals in a small field, she is likely to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and control tempo at her own discretion over this 1m½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Epsom. Celestra and Too Hot To Tango are both natural prominent types, meaning the pace picture is crowded at the front end despite the modest field size — Too Hot To Tango has been mapped to midfield and Trio pushed to the rear simply because the race shape cannot accommodate every horse in its preferred position. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berths, with Chantelle and Celestra most likely to actually hold the prominent positions while Too Hot To Tango is forced to concede ground early. A controlled, sustainable gallop set by Chantelle is the dominant expectation, which strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the straight — pure hold-up tactics from the rear are undermined by the fact that Trio, mapped there, is a redistributed prominent type rather than a genuine closer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chantelle Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Chantelle dictates an unchallenged, honest gallop and the race is decided by who tracks her most efficiently into the Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: Chantelle's uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground suits her profile and Sir Mark Prescott's patient approach off a 152-day break; horses who travel prominently without burning energy early will be best placed to challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Fades, Rivals Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Chantelle's return from 152 days off blunts her stamina late and the pressing horses overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A prominent racer who has been conserving energy just off the pace would benefit as Chantelle weakens, with Celestra's recent winning form over this trip and going profile making her the prime beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, All Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the compact field bunches throughout and produces a tight, sprint-style finish from the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: With no genuine hold-up horse in the race, all four runners are likely to be within a length or two entering the straight, making weight and raw ability the deciding factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong early and forces a blanket finish in which the horses mapped deepest rally.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally weakened because both Trio and Too Hot To Tango are natural prominent types redistributed to the rear — they are not true closers and are unlikely to execute a genuine late run from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Chantelle's 152-day absence is the single biggest variable — watch whether she moves fluently to post and how quickly she jumps, as any hesitation or rustiness could see Celestra immediately assume control of the race.

Too Hot To Tango and Trio are both natural prominent types who may instinctively push forward at the start despite their mapped positions — a scramble for position in the first two furlongs could briefly lift the tempo and compromise Chantelle's controlled lead.

The confirmed Good to Firm going at Epsom for this race (despite the header listing Good) rewards horses with proven form on a quick surface; Celestra's similar-going record of 4/6 including one win and three placings stands out, while Trio's 3/9 record is less compelling.

With only four runners, the draw and early positioning will be exaggerated — any horse that misses the break or is squeezed at the start faces an almost insurmountable task if the field compacts quickly on Epsom's unique layout.

Celestra's headgear (p — first time or returning in a hood/visor) could affect her early mannerism and how readily she settles behind Chantelle; note her behaviour in the pre-parade ring and whether she is relaxed or keen.

races.name: Spillers Winners Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has placings on good ground over this trip and, despite a hold-up profile, Daniel Muscutt may be forced to ride positively in this leaderless race, giving it a genuine chance to establish the best position in the field; sim-going record of four placings in eleven attempts without a win is a minor negative but the 7f on good suits.
runners_data.comment: Koffee And Kale has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him clear of this field, but he arrives winless in his last five starts — including a seventh last time out — and the yard is in a lean spell, making confidence measured.

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride on this consistent Rob Smyth-Osbourne-trained juvenile who has placed three times in eleven good-ground starts and has run exclusively on good ground — the going holds no fears — but a sequence of five finishes between fourth and sixth signals a horse that tries hard without quite quickening decisively, which is a concern in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Eyes Front nevertheless catches the eye with experience over today's trip and going, a sharp 14-day turnaround keeping him race-fit, and our rating of 69 suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 63 implies — the concern is he must prove he can convert that potential into a finish closer to the frame.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's charge has form over 7f on good ground including a runner-up finish, and the 5lb claim from Seamus Cronin is a useful weight relief; however, it is a genuine hold-up type placed into a midfield role on this map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed, meaning it may not get the space its style demands and its STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Credit Forgedd It returns on a quick turnaround of 14 days, has run over today's trip and going, and carries 131 lb from stall 4 — his rating of 66 marks him as a genuine danger, though he remains yet to win.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: Neil Callan is experienced enough to manufacture a bold front-grab in a field with no confirmed leader, and that tactical awareness is this horse's main claim — its form on good ground is modest (no wins, no places in six good-ground starts) and the six-furlong wins in its history suggest it may not truly stay seven furlongs at a genuine pace, but in a slow-run race that becomes a sprint it could get home.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sun Of Dolly nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround carrying 130 lb from stall 2, and our rating edges above his official mark — the fourth last time out, however, underlines he needs to find more to threaten.

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: The standout form piece in the field — a win over 7f on good going is a clear asset in this company, and Jack Channon's yard has been in fine form (T14: 4/19); the p headgear (pads) may sharpen its focus, and 30 days since last run is not a concern for this trainer; the true hold-up profile means it needs a clean run in the straight, but its finishing power is the most proven in the race.
runners_data.comment: Red Moon won three starts back but has been below that level since, finishing fifth last time out; he has run over today's trip and returns after a 30-day break, though his rating of 58 ranks him fifth of seven runners here.

runners_data.name: Imagine That
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's filly has placed twice in the last fortnight and the trainer's 2/9 T14 record shows the yard is active; 33 days between runs is the longest gap in the field, and while it handles good ground it has yet to place at Epsom or over 7f; shunted from hold-up to midfield on the map, its natural closing style means it needs the pace to collapse in front for its modest finishing effort to count.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-pack and worse efforts, Imagine That is hard to fancy from sixth in the ratings — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 33-day freshener at least means she arrives ready.

runners_data.name: Real Gold
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook and John Bridger's consistent performer has placed in three of its last four starts, all on soft or standard, and the switch to good to firm at Epsom is an unknown quantity — sim-going record of just two placings in eleven attempts flags this as a possible going concern; its relentless record of thirds suggests a horse that plugs on honestly but rarely quickens decisively enough to win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite a string of thirds, Real Gold has experience over today's trip and going, and 15 days since her last run suggests she's fresh — but ranked last on our figures, she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 121 lb.

races.paceDynamic: With all seven runners carrying a hold-up profile and the going confirmed Good to Firm at Epsom's 7f, this race has no natural front-runner to set a genuine gallop — the field will almost certainly crawl into a slow-tempo dash in the final two furlongs, turning the contest into a sprint from the home turn. Whoever can find a position closest to the pace from the break, or quicken most sharply off a slow early gallop, will hold a decisive positional advantage. The absence of any confirmed lead or prominent type means the race is entirely self-paced, with riders forced to make uncomfortable decisions about when to commit. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse with the sharpest turn of foot and the jockey best placed to read the developing tempo — a late, explosive burst from a well-positioned hold-up horse is the dominant profile, though with so many genuine hold-up types crammed into the field, the one who can secure the best tracking position through the first half of the race will gain a crucial edge. The field holds more confirmed hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear — Credit Forgedd It, Sun Of Dolly, Red Moon, Imagine That, and Real Gold are all genuine closers but several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer, with Koffee And Kale and Eyes Front most likely to find a natural rhythm nearest the front given their form patterns.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the early stages and bunches before a fierce sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With no pace to run at, horses will stalk each other before a furious scramble erupts in the straight; the horse with the quickest acceleration off the slow gallop and a clear passage will dominate. Koffee And Kale and Eyes Front, best placed to track any forward movement, are ideally suited to this dash-from-the-front-of-the-pack shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one genuine hold-up type finds an unobstructed run and delivers a powerful late surge through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: The slow early gallop compresses the field but leaves the straight wide open for a horse with real finishing speed to pick off rivals who have gone too soon; Red Moon, the only winner in the field on good ground over 7f, is best equipped to deliver that late burst. Credit Forgedd It's second at this trip on good ground also makes it a candidate if it secures a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Breaks Field
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched field encounters interference in the straight, scattering momentum and creating gaps for a quickening type.
scenarios.body: Compressed fields at Epsom's 7f often produce scrimmaging late as riders fight for running room around the home turn; the horse that finds daylight earliest and builds momentum first will steal a march on rivals who are checked or squeezed. Imagine That and Real Gold, both consistent placers in similar conditions, could capitalise if rivals cancel each other out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Front-Grab Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one rider ignores the hold-up tag and boldly takes the race by the scruff, controlling the slow gallop wire-to-wire.
scenarios.body: In a field with no natural leader, a jockey who presses to the front from the break and dictates a modest, controlled tempo could steal a march before rivals realise they are in trouble; with a small field of seven and no one designated to lead, the theft is entirely possible. Sun Of Dolly, if pushed forward by Neil Callan, and Imagine That are the likeliest opportunists in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Red Moon's hold-up profile and proven win over 7f on good ground make it the one horse in this field with the form to fire a decisive late move — watch whether George Bass can manufacture daylight turning into the straight, as a blocked passage is the only thing likely to stop it running on strongly.

With all seven runners hold-up types and no confirmed front-runner, watch for a bunched false start to the race where no rider commits early — if the gallop is dangerously slow for the first three furlongs, the race will be decided in the final 90 yards and positional luck on the day becomes critical.

Koffee And Kale and Eyes Front are both likely to be forced closer to the pace than their natural styles dictate — if either jockey misjudges the tempo and commits too early in the straight, they risk stopping in front and handing the race to a genuine finisher like Red Moon or Credit Forgedd It.

Credit Forgedd It's 5lb claim from Seamus Cronin is the most significant weight relief in the race at OR 61 — if the claim translates to track position in a slowly-run contest, it could outrun its odds, but the STYLE_FIT concern means it will likely be disadvantaged by a midfield berth rather than its preferred hold-up role.

Sun Of Dolly has no good-ground wins or places across six attempts in similar conditions — Neil Callan will need to manufacture an unexpected tactical advantage for it to feature, and punters should watch its market move late as a signal of stable confidence rather than form-based expectation.

races.name: Spillers Spectacular Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground and posted a 2nd on Soft in recent outings, making her the most in-form prominent racer here; Attwater's yard is quiet (0/8 in 14 days) but the 21-day return is comfortable, and her sim-going record (1 win, 1 place from 5) supports this surface.
runners_data.comment: Twirler arrives on the back of a second three starts back and is well treated on our rating as the top-rated runner in this field, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the concern is that her two most recent efforts have been disappointing.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner whose sim-going stats (4 from 5 on comparable ground, no wins but three places) confirm she handles this surface well; Dods stable is in form (6/28 in 14 days) and with a clean lead she will be hard to dislodge off a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Gormire has been consistently placed — second three times and third once in that sequence — and has run over today's trip and going, while her speed rating of 74 edges above her official mark; the main risk is that elusive win.

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old whose best effort was a 2nd at 6f on Standard and a 3rd on Good, suggesting the step to Good to Firm is the main question; the hood (hg: /es) may sharpen her focus and trainer Channon's yard has been placing horses with care (4/19 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Victor Cee
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has placed at 5f and 6f on Good ground but whose sim-going record (1 win, 3 places from 13) shows he handles it without dominating; the p-headgear hints at a horse who needs to be kept up to his work, and a clean run from the rear is essential.
runners_data.comment:
Victor Cee returns in good time after finishing third last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in his last six starts, but drawn in stall five carrying 129 lb, his rating of 73 makes him an appealing each-way proposition on conditions that suit.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Consistently placed (three 3rds on Good at 6f in recent history) but unable to win from 15 runs on comparable going, which brands her as a solid fill-in who lacks a finishing punch; the blinkers (hg: b) suggest connections are trying to sharpen her up, and Allen's quiet book (0/2) is not alarming given the small sample.
runners_data.comment: Elvetham has been a model of consistency, finishing third four times and second once in his last six starts, and with experience of today's trip and going, the conditions look tailor-made; the concern is he remains yet to win despite those repeated near-misses.

runners_data.name: Mount Mogan
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from a 155-day break and all five recent starts have been over 7f-8f on All-Weather, making this 6f turf return a substantial contextual shift; his recent win came at 7f on Standard and he has no sim-going turf data to lean on, so the layoff and distance drop combine as significant unknowns.
runners_data.comment: A winner in his last five starts but that came over 150 days ago, and consecutive fifth-place finishes beforehand make him hard to trust; ranked sixth of seven on our figures, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last-to-first style is well documented (1 win, 2 places from 15 on sim going), but with other hold-up types in the field he is unlikely to secure the unchallenged deep position that suits him best — his effectiveness is contingent on getting clear daylight in the straight, which this race shape does not guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's trip and going, and a win among his last six starts gives him a recent form boost, but fifth last time out and a draw from stall seven on 127 lb make this a tough ask for a 56-rated gelding.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Gormire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 6f handicap and, with no genuine rival prepared to push her for the lead, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo from the Epsom starting gates. Twirler, Sugar Sugar, and Elvetham will all press into prominent positions behind her, creating a well-organised but not overly pressured lead group, while Victor Cee, Mount Mogan, and Harry Brown operate from deeper. The going is effectively Good to Firm — faster than the headline "Good" suggests — which will sharpen early fractions and reward horses who travel economically close to the pace rather than those forced to make up ground on a quick surface. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominent in the first two or three, travel without burning energy, and sustain their effort through the Epsom straight; true hold-up horses face a stiff ask off what will be a controlled but brisk tempo on ground that dries out stamina reserves. The field holds more prominent types than can all find their natural position, and Lady Gormire and Twirler are best placed to actually secure the roles they want; Sugar Sugar and Elvetham will have to contest the same ground and one or more will be shuffled wider or slightly further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Gormire Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire leads at a sustainable clip and the prominent horses cannot close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lady Gormire's excellent sim-going record (4/5 place strikes on Good or similar) and clear front-running role on fast ground allows her to set exactly the tempo that suits her, and with no rival dedicated to running her off her feet she can conserve enough energy to repel late challenges; the Epsom 6f straight rewards a horse who has led and is still holding a rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire's pace softens enough in the final two furlongs for a prominent tracker travelling well to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Twirler has won over 6f on Good ground and carries strong recent form (placed 2nd on Soft recently, won on Good), making her the most dangerous challenger from the prominent group if she can slot in a gear change off the final bend; Sugar Sugar, placed on Good at this trip, also profiles for this shape having tracked leaders before.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop On Tired Field
scenarios.trigger: If early fractions prove faster than anticipated and the prominent group ties up, allowing deeper-tracked horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: Victor Cee has placed at this level on Good ground and would theoretically benefit from a true pace collapse, and Mount Mogan returned with a win on his comeback though his course record is confined to longer trips on AW; however, Harry Brown is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map and may not secure his ideal deep position, limiting his effectiveness even in a scenario that suits his profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Break Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If a tardy or awkward start reshuffles positions significantly and the race is run at an irregular tempo.
scenarios.body: A muddled early order could see Lady Gormire lose the lead to an accidentally-fast-breaking prominent, creating a falsely fast opening and a messy finish where positional confusion rather than class determines the result; Elvetham's consistent placed record at this course distance and trip profile means she could profit from disorder, while Twirler's course-distance winning form gives her resilience under any tempo.

watchPoints.text: Lady Gormire's ability to control the pace entirely is the pivotal factor — if she gets uncontested early lead, the race is likely hers to lose, so watch her gate break closely.

Twirler and Sugar Sugar are both prominent types who will compete for the same ground behind Lady Gormire; one or both could be inconvenienced in the first furlong, affecting their ability to travel sweetly.

Mount Mogan's 155-day absence combined with a drop to 6f on turf from recent AW middle-distance form makes his sectionals in the opening two furlongs a key read on whether he is fit enough to be competitive.

Harry Brown's redistribution to midfield on the map reflects a genuine hold-up horse unable to get his preferred rear position — watch whether Rob Hornby elects to drop him out anyway and what room he finds turning into the straight.

The going is being reported as Good to Firm for this race despite the headline Good description — any horse whose form is heavily Soft/Heavy biased should be treated with extra caution, and none of the field here raises a major alarm on that front.
